answer: Anyone can insure an identity against clonehood at a market rate, and when the identity is proved to be a clone the insurer pays out of its own reserve, which turns detection into a revenue stream for whoever performs it. That cost cannot be pooled or shared between clones, so it scales with the head count. The reef is the premium, the zephyr the underwriting pool that pays on a clone proof, and the ivory the correlated funding that sets the price; the reef scales with the ivory, and the zephyr only pays when the clone is actually proved.
